report: ring110k with sleep=on looked less stable than sleep=off: settled bodies jolted when woken, in waves.
causes: Sleepers never query the broadphase, so pairs between two sleepers and between a sleeper and static geometry were never emitted. Their warm-start history (lambda, penalties) was lost while asleep; a woken body restarted those contacts cold and sagged, waking its neighbours in turn.

The exact small-scene broadphase (<= 512 colliders) dropped awake-sleeper pairs when the sleeper had the lower index (lower index owns the pair, but sleepers never query). A woken body fell straight through a sleeping body below it; the grid path already had this exception.
change: carry_rest_pairs (HOST_S(28), work slot 72 = previous GPU manifold count) re-emits last step's manifolds whose bodies are both at rest (static or sleeping) as candidates, after the broadphase and before narrowphase overwrites gManifolds; slot 64 is recounted. Narrowphase reuses them through the existing at-rest path, which copies contacts unchanged, so lambda/k stay frozen while asleep. Sleepers no longer emit rest pairs themselves (small path, large-body list) to avoid duplicates. The small-path ownership rule now exempts sleeping partners. Browser default rest=carry (rest=drop keeps the control); native ENGINE_REST=carry. HOST_S(27)/(28) flags are WGSL-only because Metal reads host slots from gScratchAtomics, whose words 26+ hold the large-body list.
wakeTest: waking_a_sleeping_stack_does_not_jolt_or_cascade: one woken top box in 3 columns (small path, per-contact hash) and 64 columns (grid, record hash) moves 0.51 mm with carry vs 0.80 mm cold, against 0.40 mm creep for a stack that never sleeps; limit 1.5x creep + 50 um, no neighbour may wake, and the cold restart must exceed the limit. Before the small-path fix the woken box fell 6.9 m.
